classification.difficultyReason: Construct equal unit intervals and mark whole numbers, with the hardest part applying two strict bounds and excluding both endpoints.

content.prompt: For each of the following, draw a number line from 0 to 10.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Mark the numbers 2, 4, 6 and 8 on it.

answer.worked: Draw equally spaced ticks labelled 0 to 10. Place a dot at each of 2, 4, 6 and 8.

spec.description: Equally spaced whole-number ticks from 0 to 10 with closed points at 2, 4, 6 and 8.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Mark the numbers 1, 3, 5 and 7 on it.

answer.worked: Draw equally spaced ticks labelled 0 to 10. Place a dot at each of 1, 3, 5 and 7.

spec.description: Equally spaced whole-number ticks from 0 to 10 with closed points at 1, 3, 5 and 7.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Mark the whole numbers less than 5 on it.

answer.worked: Whole numbers start at 0. The whole numbers less than 5 are 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4. Draw equally spaced ticks labelled 0 to 10 and place dots at these five numbers.

spec.description: Equally spaced whole-number ticks from 0 to 10 with closed points at 0 through 4.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Mark the whole numbers less than 8 and greater than 2 on it.

answer.worked: The whole numbers strictly between 2 and 8 are 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7. Draw equally spaced ticks labelled 0 to 10 and place dots at these five numbers; exclude 2 and 8.

spec.description: Equally spaced whole-number ticks from 0 to 10 with closed points at 3 through 7.
